senses: Having a spline or splines.
Any of a group of tough, leathery poroid mushrooms similar to boletes but typically lacking a distinct stalk.
Such residue from apples used in the process of cidermaking; also, a mass of crushed apples before the juice is pressed out.
Such residue from grapes used in winemaking.
Such residue (especially castor bean cake or fish scrap) used as fertilizer.
ety: [Alt: Red grape flesh and seeds] From Late Middle English pomis, pomys (“cider; pulp of plants pressed to extract their juice or oil”), probably from Medieval Latin pōmācium, pōmātium (“cider”), possibly a variant of pomaceum (although first attested later), from Latin pōmum (“fruit; fruit tree”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó (“away; off”) + *h₁em- (“to take”), in the sense of something taken off a tree) + -āceum (neuter form of -āceus (suffix meaning ‘belonging to; having the nature of’, forming adjectives)). Doublet of pomade, pomate, and pomatum. Sense 1.1 (“crushed apples”) a

senses: Biochemistry (science or industry).
ety: Clipping of biochemistry. Analyzable as bio- (“biological”) + chem (“chemistry”) or as a clipped compound, bio(logical) chem(istry).

senses: The making and launching of rockets, its science and practice.
examples: Sustained research in rocketry had at last succeeded in attaining one of its objectives. It had sent up a missile which stayed up. It was, in fact, possible to fire a rocket far enough up for it to fall into an orbit.

senses: A child who is able to creep using its hands and knees but is not able to walk.
A tractor crawler, a motorized vehicle that uses caterpillar tracks instead of wheels.
A software bot that autonomously follows connected paths such as links between web pages.
A mobile stage in the development of stationary hemipteran insects such as scale insects—generally the first instar.
Synonym of crawler crane.
ety: From crawl (“to move slowly, by dragging the body along the ground”) + -er.
examples: Crawler-based search engines have three major elements. The first is the spider, also called the crawler, which visits a web page, reads it, and then follows links to other pages within the site.
These serve as an algorithmic way to judge the “mobileness” of a site, and similar algorithms are likely to be used by the search crawlers.

senses: A person skilled in horology, particularly a person who makes or repairs timekeeping devices.
A hybrid organism of this kind.
An area which is considered particularly low or lower than surrounding areas.
examples: The lowland region was prone to flooding during the rainy season.

senses: Of the period following a war.
Of the period following the American Civil War, especially used in reference to the South.
ety: From Latin post bellum (literally “after the war”).
examples: For most Europeans, a postbellum world had seemed the self-evident future, says Finland’s president, Sauli Niinistö.

senses: Any of a number of Australian eucalyptus trees with fibrous bark, or the wood or bark of such trees.
examples: Two of the younger men carried him there on a stretcher of stringybark.

senses: one-dimensional
One who has committed the act of arson, or illegally setting fire to property.
Fitted with a gasket.
The ordinal form of the number one trillion.
A fat person.
Fatness, fat; podginess.
ety: Perhaps from pudsy (“plump”), which could be a diminutive of pud (“child's hand, forepaw”).

senses: A conversion to the use of the metric system; a metrification.
examples: In these days of decimalization and metrication it is a pity that SI units were not used as this will date a very useful little book prematurely.

senses: The state or condition of being a subscriber.
A small conical pile of hay, or a heap of hay thrown up in a hayfield while the hay is being cured or awaiting relocation to a haystack or barn.
ety: From Middle English haycok, hacoke, haycoke; equivalent to hay + cock (“conical heap”).
examples: And then in haste her bow'r she leaves, With Thestylis to bind the sheaves; Or if the earlier season lead To the tann'd haycock in the mead.
And willows, willow-herb, and grass, / And meadowsweet, and haycocks dry, / No whit less still and lonely fair / Than the high cloudlets in the sky.

senses: A trained musician who plays percussion instruments, as opposed to a drummer who lacks formal training.
examples: Since the 1960s, the keyboardist, vibraphonist and percussionist Mulatu Astatke has been a prime mover in Ethio-jazz: unmistakably Ethiopian music that also draws on American jazz, Afro-Caribbean music and more.

senses: A themed collection of similar toys designed to work together to enact some action or event.
A unitary structure for children to play on, typically including a slide, and often swings, ropes to climb on, and other things found as separate structures at public playgrounds.
examples: Your children can play on the small playset, climb through a hollow log, and draw a picture for all to see.

senses: Capable of being located.
The branch of anthropology that compares and analyzes different human cultures and the relationships between them.
A subtitle that has been burned into a video file's frames.
A person who writes satire.
examples: In one of the Greek satirist Lucian's Dialogues of Courtesans, a conversation takes place between the hetaira Tryphaena and a young client named Charmides.

senses: The awarding of a match to a wrestler after their opponent has been counted out (usually after ten seconds of being outside the ring) by the referee.
A person who rides a skateboard.
Any vast prairie bordering a desert.
ety: Originates from the Khoikhoi word karo (meaning dry, and hard)

senses: A thick soup, especially a creamy one.
ety: Borrowed from French potage, and from earlier borrowing pottage.

senses: An act of rescinding: removing, taking away, or taking back.
ety: 1651, Late Latin rescissio, from Latin rescindō (“to cut back”), from re- (“back”) + scindō (“to cut”).

senses: Resembling or relating to rheumatism.
Derived from, or having the character of, rheum; rheumic.
ety: From Middle French rheumatique, from Latin rheumaticus, from Ancient Greek ῥευματικός (rheumatikós), from ῥεῦμα (rheûma, “stream, flow”) from ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow”).

senses: To refill (an appliance such as an air-conditioning unit) with the gases needed for operation.
examples: If your air conditioner has stopped working, you may need to regas it.

senses: A council, assembly, or public meeting, in some Muslim countries or territories.
The parliament of Iran.
A cabalistic method of interpreting Hebrew words, based on numerical values of letters.
ety: From Aramaic גִּימַטְרְיָא (gīmāṭrəyā), from Ancient Greek γεωμετρία (geōmetría, “geometry”). Doublet of geometry.

senses: One of several tangy green vegetables used in Japanese cuisine, usually Brassica rapa var. nipposinica
examples: His cold sesame chicken seasoned with chili is finely shredded and served in carefully wrought clusters around a salad of mizuna.

senses: A small restaurant, tavern or shop in the Caucasus and Crimea.
A swordsman.
ety: From Middle English swerdman; equivalent to sword + -man.
examples: Worthy fellows, and like to prove most sinewy swordmen

senses: having a specified form of wit (intellectual ability)
ety: From Middle English witted, ywitted, equivalent to wit + -ed. Compare Old English witod (“appointed, ordained, assured, certain”).

senses: equalitarian
A rice croquette filled with mozzarella or meat, originally from Rome.
ety: Borrowed from Italian supplì, from French surprise, because of the supposedly unexpected filling. Doublet of surprise.
